title: Aft Pylon Fairing — Installation
abstract: Installation of the aft pylon fairing, including the seal compression check at six points, the latch load measurement and the ground run witness-mark inspection that proves the interface is closed.

sections.purpose: This task installs the aft pylon fairing on the pylon and proves that the interface seal is compressed correctly around its whole perimeter, which is what keeps exhaust gas out of the fairing cavity.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the engine installed and the thrust reverser still deactivated. The seal compression check is done with the fairing latched but before the ground run; a fairing that closes easily is usually a fairing whose seal is not compressed. The latch load must be measured with the spring balance, not judged by feel, and the limits table has one column because one seal is fitted. Allow for a ground run at the end of the task.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the pylon interface is clean and that the drain line behind the fairing is clear. 2. With three persons, lift the fairing onto the hinge line and install the hinge clevis pins EN169671-8B. 3. Connect the bonding lead and do a bonding resistance check. 4. Install the fairing maintenance stay and lower the fairing onto it. 5. Install or check the interface seal and put a witness paste bead at six points around the perimeter. 6. Close the fairing and latch it in the sequence marked on the fairing, inner pair first. 7. Measure the latch load at each latch with the spring balance and compare against the limits table. WARNING: A LATCH LOAD ABOVE THE UPPER LIMIT MEANS THE SEAL IS OVER-COMPRESSED AND THE LUG KIT MAY BE PRELOADED. DO NOT RELEASE THE AIRCRAFT. 8. Open the fairing and read the witness paste at all six points. Every point must show contact over at least 6 mm of bead width. CAUTION: A BEAD THAT SHOWS CONTACT ON ONE EDGE ONLY IS NOT A PASS. THE SEAL IS TWISTED AND WILL EXTRUDE IN SERVICE. 9. Correct any point that does not show contact by re-working the lower fairing lug kit ROD165267-21 to the dimension on the drawing. 10. Close and latch the fairing. 11. Do a ground run at the power setting given in the accomplishment instructions and inspect the interface for witness marks afterwards.
sections.close_out: Reactivate the thrust reverser and remove the tag. Remove the access platform and the maintenance stay. Record the latch loads, the seal compression result and the ground run inspection in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Keep the thrust reverser deactivated until the task is complete.
Do not stand under the fairing while it is on the stay.
Use ear protection during the ground run.

title: Aft Pylon Fairing — Installation

issue.reason: The seal compression limits are split by seal thickness, the ventilated shield standoff check is inserted before the fairing is closed, and the shield fastener sequence is given.

abstract: Installation of the aft pylon fairing, including the seal compression check at six points, the latch load measurement and the ground run witness-mark inspection that proves the interface is closed.

sections.purpose: This task installs the aft pylon fairing on the pylon and proves that the interface seal is compressed correctly around its whole perimeter, which is what keeps exhaust gas out of the fairing cavity.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the engine installed and the thrust reverser still deactivated. The seal compression check is done with the fairing latched but before the ground run; a fairing that closes easily is usually a fairing whose seal is not compressed. The limits table now has two columns. The delivered 6 mm seal takes a latch load of 180 to 240 N and shows a 6 mm witness bead; the 9 mm seal fitted with the ventilated heat shield takes 240 to 320 N and shows a 9 mm bead, because the thicker section has to be compressed further to seal against the same land. Reading the wrong column will either condemn a correct installation or release an over-compressed one. The shield fastener sequence also changes with the thicker seal: the shield is now pulled down at the two centre bosses first so that the standoffs seat square before the corners are drawn in. Allow for a ground run at the end of the task.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the pylon interface is clean and that the drain line behind the fairing is clear. 2. With three persons, lift the fairing onto the hinge line and install the hinge clevis pins EN169671-8B. 3. Connect the bonding lead and do a bonding resistance check. 4. Install the fairing maintenance stay and lower the fairing onto it. 5. Where the ventilated heat shield is fitted, check the standoff dimension at each boss on the upper doubler JAR270491-60 before the fairing is closed, and tighten the shield fasteners at the two centre bosses first, then the corners, in the sequence on the drawing. CAUTION: A COLLAPSED STANDOFF BOSS CLOSES THE AIR GAP AND THE SHIELD STOPS WORKING. 6. Install or check the interface seal, confirm its thickness against the aircraft standard, and put a witness paste bead at six points around the perimeter. 7. Close the fairing and latch it in the sequence marked on the fairing, inner pair first. 8. Measure the latch load at each latch with the spring balance and compare against the column of the limits table for the seal fitted. WARNING: A LATCH LOAD ABOVE THE UPPER LIMIT MEANS THE SEAL IS OVER-COMPRESSED AND THE LUG KIT MAY BE PRELOADED. DO NOT RELEASE THE AIRCRAFT. 9. Open the fairing and read the witness paste at all six points. Every point must show contact over the bead width for the seal fitted. 10. Correct any point that does not show contact by re-working the lower fairing lug kit ROD165267-21 to the dimension on the drawing. 11. Close and latch the fairing. 12. Do a ground run at the power setting given in the accomplishment instructions and inspect the interface for witness marks afterwards.
sections.close_out: Reactivate the thrust reverser and remove the tag. Remove the access platform and the maintenance stay. Record the seal thickness fitted, the limits column used, the latch loads, the seal compression result and the ground run inspection in the aircraft technical log.

type_data.effectivity_note: Auran-powered SLN-30R3 and SLN-34R3 aircraft; step 5 and the 9 mm seal column apply to aircraft post MOD-131340 only

safety_precautions: Keep the thrust reverser deactivated until the task is complete.
Do not stand under the fairing while it is on the stay.
Use ear protection during the ground run.
